entities.name: Girim of Silla
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Girim (reigned 298–310 CE), also known as Girip and Gigu, served as the fifteenth monarch of the ancient Korean kingdom of Silla. His reign, though relatively brief, is primarily remembered for a pivotal semantic shift: the formal adoption of "Silla" (新羅) as the official name of the kingdom, replacing earlier designations. This act, recorded in the foundational historical text *Samguk Sagi*, marked a significant step in the consolidation of Silla's identity and its emergence as a distinct political entity on the Korean Peninsula. Though his paternal lineage traced back to the Park clan, Girim was counted among the Seok kings due to his mother's prominent Seok heritage, reflecting the complex, often fluid, inter-clan power dynamics that characterized early Silla's royal succession.

During his twelve-year rule, King Girim continued the state-building efforts initiated by his predecessors, navigating the internal politics of competing aristocratic clans and external pressures from neighboring polities. While specific military campaigns or grand architectural projects are not prominently detailed in extant records, his reign solidified the administrative groundwork for future expansion. The most enduring act attributed to him was the declaration of "Silla" as the kingdom's name in 307 CE. This was not merely a linguistic change; it represented a conscious effort to project a more unified and definitive image of the burgeoning state, moving away from less formal or regional appellations.
